briefing.opening: Good morning. Welcome to the climate briefing for August 25, 2026. Today's climate-related news, collected globally, presents a complex picture where extreme climate phenomena intersect with our efforts to respond to them.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Climate Crisis: A Global Warning
sections.content: Europe has recently faced scorching heatwaves, described as 'unlivable without air conditioning' [1], suggesting that climate change has become a harsh reality [70]. The American Southwest is also experiencing a record-breaking heat dome, exposing over 45 million people to dangerous high temperatures [99], and these heatwaves are highly likely to be closely linked to climate change [61]. Domestically, concerns are rising about food shortages due to heatwaves [13], and climate change is severely impacting the 'world's cherry capital' [65] as well as European crop and feed supplies [80]. Furthermore, an analysis indicates that major carbon polluters are half responsible for the water crisis in the Western U.S. [62, 77], and calls for strengthening water security are also continuing domestically [10]. Such simultaneous occurrences of four typhoons [88] and extreme climate phenomena like 'Super El Niño' are threatening energy security [92] and increasing dangerous flight incidents [97], signaling a global emergency [100].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 The Reality of Carbon Neutrality Implementation and Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts are ongoing to transition to a carbon-neutral society. Goyang and Wonju cities are strengthening citizen education through climate environment schools and carbon neutrality academies [4, 15, 20, 25], and Anseong City's Carbon Neutrality Citizen Action Group showed high participation in the Energy Day lights-out event [16]. Asan City Council has formed a special committee on carbon neutrality, demonstrating active commitment by reviewing policies across city administration and identifying new projects [22, 23, 26, 29, 38]. Corporations also recognize the importance of an eco-friendly image, with Amore and Pulmuone collaborating with the government to launch campaigns promoting carbon-neutral consumption [30, 32, 35]. However, challenges persist in energy transition policies. While efforts to expand renewable energy continue, such as the Ministry of Climate discussing renewable energy procurement methods with global semiconductor companies [5, 51, 55] and Haenam County establishing guidelines for sharing development profits from new and renewable energy [44, 46, 50], concerns are also being raised about power shortages during evening peak hours due to the intermittency of solar power generation [57, 58]. Moreover, with the government's push to expand LNG power generation, an additional 69.8 million tons of greenhouse gases are projected to be emitted annually by 2035 [19, 60], highlighting a discrepancy with carbon neutrality goals. Additionally, in the UK, two new data centers are expected to emit more carbon than ExxonMobil's entire UK operations [102], making public-private cooperation for expanding renewable energy to meet the increasing power demand of advanced industries even more urgent [41].

sections.title: 🌱 Climate Change Adaptation and Education: Efforts for the Future
sections.content: Amidst the threat of climate change, positive movements through adaptation and education are active. Domestically, attempts are being made to overcome reduced pear export volumes due to climate change through 'data farming' [2], and in Cheorwon, innovation in agricultural technology for climate change response is accelerating [7]. GS E&C is collaborating with architect Carlo Ratti to research 'future homes' and residential solutions that respond to the climate crisis [8, 11, 12, 14], and in Gyeongnam, efforts to improve infrastructure, such as expanding groundwater storage dams to cope with drought, are also underway [9]. Citizen participation is also active, with the Basal Unjeong Seon-gun Association holding a resolution rally for climate change response [3], and 200 citizens at the Goyang City Climate Environment School receiving education on seeking carbon neutrality in daily life [4, 6, 15]. Internationally, a non-profit organization in Maine has launched a $20 million fund to help farmers adapt to climate change [67], and preparations for future generations are also being made, such as the development of guidelines for climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction education for preschoolers [87]. Furthermore, research is underway on whether AI can help plant breeders stay ahead of climate change [76].

sections.title: 🌍 Widespread Impacts of the Climate Crisis and International Discussions
sections.content: Climate change extends beyond mere weather phenomena, exerting widespread impacts across ecosystems, the economy, and society as a whole, and international discussions on this are deepening. The interconnections between biodiversity, land degradation, and Loss & Damage are being emphasized in the context of climate change [68], and research has also been published indicating that the omega-3 fatty acid content in fish and the organisms they eat could be halved [69]. The Panama Canal's struggles with severe drought [73] demonstrate that climate change can directly impact the global economy. Meanwhile, there are criticisms that the phenomenon of 'Greenhushing,' where companies remain silent about climate change, has harmful effects [66], and a pessimistic view also exists that the fight against climate change is like 'a half-empty glass' [64, 81]. However, research suggesting that seagrass and ocean carbon storage could have significant potential in reducing climate change [91, 95] offers new hope, and there are also reports of numerous positive change initiatives worldwide that can inspire and prompt action [103].

briefing.closing: As you have seen in today's briefing, the global climate crisis is sounding a serious alarm, but at the same time, various adaptation and mitigation efforts are actively underway both domestically and internationally to address it. Emphasizing once again that a deep understanding of the complexity of climate change, coupled with science-based policy decisions and active participation from civil society, are essential elements for a sustainable future, I conclude today's climate briefing.
